text:
A: Hiya! You're the quiet lad with the hi-vis in the wardrobe. I'm Kerry, Swindon.
B: Ha, yeah, that's me. Rayhan. I'm in Ilford, East London.
A: So are you on a site, then? Building?
B: Erm, sort of. I'm an apprentice electrician, final year. Mostly houses, rewires, kitchens, extensions. Bit of shop fit-out sometimes.
A: No way! My husband's a sparky. Dan. Self-employed, round Swindon. So I know all about it, believe me. The van takes up the whole drive, there's cable in my kitchen drawers.
B: Ha, that sounds about right. My boss's van is the same, except it's always on empty.
A: Oh, Dan's is always on empty and all. What is it with electricians? Are you going self-employed, then, when you're done?
B: Eventually, yeah, I'd like to. I've got my AM2 first, that's the final assessment. Then inspection and testing. Maybe my own van in my mid-twenties, me and a mate.
A: Right. Well, honestly, do it. Dan's doing alright and he's terrible at the business side. Like he's a brilliant electrician, but quotes, invoices, chasing people for money, he's useless. I sort of do all that for him, or I tell him how to word things. That's literally my job, I'm business development for a building and roofing supplier. I sit on the phone and get contractors to open accounts with us. You want someone like me on your side when you go out on your own, do you know what I mean?
B: Yeah, that makes sense. I'm alright with the paperwork side, I keep my job notes and test sheets neat. It's more like getting customers that worries me.
A: That's the easy bit! You just ring people. Find out who signs off the money and talk to them, not the receptionist. Don't waste your time being nice to the wrong person.
B: Erm, okay. I'd probably still be nice to the receptionist though.
A: Ha. Fair enough, you're sweet. Where do you get your stuff from, Screwfix?
B: Mostly, yeah. Or the wholesaler the firm uses. The tool prices at Screwfix are mad, though.
A: See, that's where a trade account comes in. You get the discounts. I do Dan's discounts, he never even asks, he just pays what's on the shelf.
B: Yeah, my boss has got one. I just use his.
A: Use his while you can, mate. So what do you do when you're not wiring things?
B: Football Thursday, five-a-side. Gym some mornings. Watch Arsenal. Family stuff at weekends, there's always a wedding or something.
A: Oh, I love a wedding. We had ours near Marlborough, big do at a hotel, honestly better than anyone else's I've been to. Free bar till ten.
B: That sounds nice.
A: It was. Are you seeing anyone, then? Are they on at you about getting married?
B: Erm. A bit, yeah. My brother got married last year, so now everyone's looking at me. I'm not ready, I want to qualify first.
A: Good for you. Don't let them rush you. Everyone's always asking me when I'm having kids, I'm like, mind your own.
B: Yeah. That's it really.
A: Did you do that puzzle at the start? I thought it was a bit pointless, to be honest.
B: Erm, I didn't mind it. I was tired, I'd just come in from work.
A: Oh, I'm knackered and all, I've been on the phone all day. Right, well, when you get your van, look me up. Swindon's not that far.
B: Ha, yeah. Thanks. I'll remember that.
